note: Mechanical repairs applied to compiler output so a package can ship before upstream fixes the emitter. A repair may only correct TEXT. It may never change absence, reference identity, equality, ordering, exception shape, or task settlement -- those are the contract in AGENTS.md, and a semantic repair is a lie that our own tests would then certify. Every repair declares the upstream defect it stands in for, and `npm run sdk:check` fails when a repair stops matching anything, so a repair cannot outlive the bug it answers. Two kinds exist. A declared `insert-forward-declaration` entry below names a symbol the emitter omits. The duplicate-structural-struct aliasing in scripts/emissionRepairs.mjs needs no entry because it is derived entirely from the emitted tree: it finds an anonymous structural struct defined in more than one package namespace with BYTE-IDENTICAL bodies, keeps the flight::types definition, and turns every other copy into a type alias to it. It reports what it aliased in manifest.duplicateStructuralStructAliases, and it is self-expiring -- when the emitter stops duplicating these, it finds nothing and rewrites nothing.

repairs.diagnostic: couldn't deduce template parameter 'T'
repairs.defect: flight::Ref<Value> resolves through detail::reference_shape<Value, complete_probe<Value>>, a computation, so a template parameter appearing only inside it is in a NON-DEDUCED CONTEXT. Every generated signal and node helper is declared that way -- template <typename T> void emit_signal(flight::Ref<flight::types::Signal<T>>, ArgsPack&&...) -- so the declaration is well-formed and the file compiles alone, while every CALL fails to deduce T. That is why packages which are 100% emitted still have failing headers: @flighthq/camera is 21/21 emitted and three of its headers fail only here, through flight/log/log.hpp's two emit_signal calls.
repairs.expires: when the emitter writes a deducible spelling for a reference parameter inside a function template -- std::shared_ptr<X> for a ReferenceEnabled X, or X itself otherwise -- instead of the flight::Ref alias; sdk:check fails if this repair matches no file.

repairs.sourceDeclaration: packages/types/src/Node.ts:19 -- export interface Node<Traits extends object = NodeTraits> extends NodeTraits, Entity
repairs.diagnostic: type/value mismatch at argument 1 in template parameter list for 'flight::Ref'; note: expected a type, got 'Node'
repairs.defect:
TypeScript's Node declares a DEFAULT type parameter (Traits extends object = NodeTraits), so a bare `Node` in the source means Node<NodeTraits>. The emitter drops the default from the generated template and then writes the bare name in template-argument position, which is not a type in C++. Five occurrences in flight/node/hierarchy.hpp, all inside flight::Ref<...>.

The argument is spelled flight::Ref<flight::types::NodeTraits> because that is how the emitter itself spells this instantiation everywhere it does supply the argument -- eight occurrences of Node<flight::Ref<flight::types::NodeTraits>> in the tree, and none of a bare Node<NodeTraits>.
